correctness.rationale: A fault-created face must contain two distinct diagonal vertices. An off-diagonal vertex compatible with both has those two indices as its coordinates; the two possible off-diagonal vertices conflict with each other, and neither can accompany a third diagonal vertex. This gives exactly the row and column simplices, the diagonal clique complex, and the stated fault triangles. Decreasing the size of the off-diagonal subset leaves its union with the row or column root as its unique coface at each prescribed removal; the triangle-edge and subsequent pendant-edge pairs are also free. In the resulting core, choose a tree in the 1-skeleton of each clique component spanning all attachment vertices (subdivide to include a chosen basepoint if needed), then add a tree on the components using c−1 intercomponent edges. Quotienting by this contractible CW subcomplex is a homotopy equivalence and leaves the component quotients and 2q−c+1 circle cells. This also identifies the inclusion on positive-degree integral homology, including torsion. The proof applies to disconnected H, n=2, and the complete or empty fault graphs. A separately constructed n=3, one-fault example yielded 37 independent faces, 10 checked elementary collapse pairs, and the exact 17-face target, counting the empty face. The frozen verifier was inspected, not executed; its recorded larger run is finite corroboration only.
